handoff.salientSummary: Fixed the stale public availability ETag: a date with no rsv_day_versions row now reads as version 0, so the first write (booking, hold, special day) changes the ETag and the old If-None-Match returns 200. Pacing and service-availability writes now bump the whole booking horizon. Operator availability now checks max_parties (and rolling caps) through the same check the booking write path uses. Full tenant-api suite passes (2520 tests).
handoff.whatWasImplemented: (1) rsv-public-engine.ts readDayVersion returns 0 when no row exists (first write stores 1). rsv-setup-crud.ts gets bumpBookingHorizonDayVersions (today..horizonDays, capped at 366), called from create/update/delete pacing rule and upsert/delete service availability, because those writes only bumped dates that already had bookings, leaving fresh dates with a stale ETag. Bookings, holds, special days and blocks already bumped through bumpDayVersion* and are fixed by the 0-default. (2) New services/rsv-operator-pacing.ts holds ACTIVE_OCCUPANCY_STATUSES and findOperatorPacingBreaches (per-bucket maxCovers and maxParties, service and window filtering) extracted from the booking write path. rsv-booking-service.ts now uses it (same error codes pacing_exceeded and pacing_parties_exceeded). getOperatorAvailability in rsv-day-feed-service.ts computes pacingWarning from that helper plus evaluatePacing (rolling cap and exact-slot caps), counting only reservations in active occupancy statuses, so available=false whenever the write would 409.

cases.name: changes the ETag on the very first write for a never-mutated date, so the old tag gets 200 (VAL-CROSS-007)
cases.verifies: Fresh date reads dayVersion 0, If-None-Match 304; after the first hold the old tag gets 200, dayVersion 1 and a new ETag.

cases.name: changes the ETag on the first special-day write for a fresh date (VAL-CROSS-007)
cases.verifies: Creating a closed special day through the operator setup route on a never-mutated date changes the ETag, old tag gets 200 with status closed.

cases.name: changes the ETag on a never-mutated date after a pacing rule or service availability write
cases.verifies: Pacing rule create and service-availability upsert each change the public ETag on a date with no bookings.

cases.name: operator availability flags a max_parties breach the same way the booking write rejects it
cases.verifies: With maxParties=1 and an existing 19:00 booking, availability reports pacingWarning=true/available=false at 19:00 only, and the booking write returns 409 pacing_parties_exceeded.

tests.coverage: ETag first-write behavior for holds, special days, pacing rules and service availability on fresh dates; operator availability max_parties parity with the write path.

discoveredIssues.description: The engine pacing mapper (booking-service, day-feed, setup-service) passes bucketMin as windowMinutes, which evaluatePacing ignores (it reads bucketMin), so the engine's slot caps use exact-slot buckets. The operator write path's explicit bucket check is what enforces bucketed caps. Left unchanged to keep behavior identical; worth aligning in a later cleanup.
